resolutions.note: Root cause was validating type without domain. Guard extended in the same place to `isinstance(v, bool) or not isinstance(v, (int, float)) or not (0 <= v < 100)`, matching the neighbouring `0 < hurdle < 1` idiom. `not (0 <= v < 100)` rejects NaN for free (all NaN comparisons are False), both infinities, and negatives in one expression; the type test stays first because `0 <= "0.585" < 100` raises rather than returning False. Upper bound 100 is where friction/100 reaches 1.0 — the widest gap two 0..1 scores can produce — so at or above it the gate is an unconditional refusal, not a strict policy; interval left half-open and 0 allowed, since zero-friction is a legitimate commission-free setting. The round-1 self-reported negative-friction debt is closed by this same guard and was not logged separately. Orchestrator verified: .nan/.inf/-.inf/-10.0/100.0 all REJECTED; 0.0/0.585/99.9 valid and still gating a 0.067 gap against a 0.15 hurdle; all three shipped examples/ips-*.md still validate.
